title: How Steve Jobs reacted to leaving Apple: "I want to build things" (Newsweek, 1985)
summary: Weeks after leaving Apple, Jobs explains why he wants to keep making things rather than become a pundit or professor, how he measures success by raising the bar for computers, and how he coped with the humiliation. He says Apple lives in its people's spirit and that he is not bitter.

principles.text: Builders should keep building; don't drift into commentary or teaching when you're best at making things.
principles.quote: I personally, man, I want to build things. I’m thirty. I’m not ready to be an industry pundit.

principles.text: His core strength: gather talented people and make things with them.
principles.quote: What I’m best at doing is finding a group of talented people and making things with them.

principles.text: If no place exists to make things, create your own place, as he did twice before.
principles.quote: And if there’s no place for me to make things there, then I’ll do what I did twice before. I’ll make my own place.

principles.text: Measure success by the lasting standard you set, not by numbers.
principles.quote: My yardstick may be how every computer that’s designed from here on out will have to be at least as good as a Macintosh.

principles.text: A company is its people's spirit and philosophy; losing it means losing the romance and sense of wonder about the product.
principles.quote: To me, Apple exists in the spirit of the people that work there, and the sort of philosophies and purpose by which they go about their business.

principles.text: In setbacks, relax, step away, and keep growing without bitterness.
principles.quote: If you relax, you’ll start breathing again. That’s how I felt all summer long. The thing I had to do was try to relax.
